headline: Hostage Rescue Exercise Declared "Technically Successful," Definition of Success Under Urgent Review

image.alt: Picture of the village before attack

body.text: In news that has shocked absolutely no one who was actually there, a joint hostage rescue exercise involving II Squadron RAF Regiment, 1 Tactical Policing and Security Squadron (1TPSS) and 4 Police Squadron RAF Police concluded this week with what organisers are calling "a broadly positive outcome for most participants."

Radio traffic throughout the exercise was, by every account, a masterclass in volume over content. One signaller described the net as "busier than a Belarusian hardbass rave and roughly as informative," adding that at several points it was genuinely unclear whether units were reporting contact or simply talking over one another for the sake of it. Attempts to establish a clear picture from anyone in a position of authority reportedly went unanswered for the entire duration, leading one junior NCO to observe that "not knowing what's going on was, if anything, the most consistent part of the plan."

Cross-unit communication fared little better. Elements on the ground are understood to have operated on the working assumption that other call signs simply did not exist, a theory apparently reinforced when at least one unit advanced into the objective area before the airmobile insertion had actually happened, arriving to a fight that, strictly speaking, hadn't been delivered to them yet.

The insertion itself was further hampered by helicopters taking a leisurely five minutes or more to descend from hover to touchdown, a figure the loadmaster insisted was "well within tolerances," without specifying whose tolerances, or for what.
Hostile civilian role-players added their own flourish, producing rifles with a suddenness several observers called "genuinely impressive," and rather more impressive than the response it provoked.

II Squadron's parachute insertion, meanwhile, achieved the rare distinction of arriving even later than 1TPSS, prompting some debate on the ground as to whether the drop was in support of the operation or a private attempt to recreate Operation Market Garden. The insertion is understood to have gone largely to plan otherwise, save for one detail: an RAF Police officer sustained a gunshot wound, believed to be friendly fire, during the approach. The officer is recovering well, and is understood to have been seen promptly by Medical Services Branch, whose presence throughout the exercise was, by all accounts, entirely professional and mercifully drama-free. II Squadron have declined to comment further, though Fish News should clarify this may simply be because nobody has actually asked them, or because someone else was talking over them on the net at the time.

By contrast, the rest of RAF Regiment, alongside 1TPSS and 4PS, acquitted themselves competently throughout, a fact one anonymous trainee — whose voice and posting were instantly recognisable to everyone present — summarised as "not a total shambles, which I'll take."

Overhead, four reconnaissance drones monitored a single village whose entire population could, by conservative estimate, have fitted comfortably into a single Fiat 500, with room left over for luggage. A senior officer defended the deployment as "prudent redundancy," a phrase Fish News notes is doing a great deal of work.
Fish News will continue to monitor the situation with its usual rigorous impartiality, and looks forward to the "lessons learned" document being quietly filed somewhere nobody will read it.
